question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]\}
$$

Consider the subspace $\text{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $B$ are given above. Given that $B$ is derived from $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\frac{b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$  

First, let's denote

$\,$ ${a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ 

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

**Step 1**: We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**: Next, we find ${v}_{2}$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for ${v}_{2}$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{2\cdot 1+5\cdot (-1)+6\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ 6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6 \\ 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $B=\{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}\}=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\}$ is an orthogonal basis for $\text{Col}(A).$

Finally, $b=6,$ $c=5,$ and  

$$
\frac{b}{c}=\frac{6}{5}.
$$
